title: Inmate, 24, from Ottawa, dies in CSC custody at Joyceville Institution in Kingston
subtitle: Donald Musselman, 24, of Ottawa, had been serving an indeterminate life sentence for second degree murder since May 2024.
article: An inmate, 24, originally from Ottawa died in Correctional Service of Canada custody in Kingston on Tuesday.

Donald Musselman was serving an indeterminate sentence for second-degree murder at Joyceville Institution when he died. CSC said his next of kin have been notified of his passing and the service will be reviewing the circumstances of his passing. CSC said Musselman's cause of death was unavailable on Tuesday. Police and the office of the coroner have also been notified.

Earlier this year, Musselman was convicted of the murder of Ottawa hip-hop artist Markland Campbell on June 7, 2019. Campbell, 42, and his daughter were in Ottawa's ByWard Market when she told him she was being harassed. Campbell confronted a group of teenagers and was shot twice defending his daughter.

According to the Ottawa Citizen, Campbell performed under the stage name Jahiant Jahh with HalfSizeGiants, an Ottawa hip-hop collective. The collective promoted non-violence and was set to return to national recognition after a 10-year hiatus when Campbell was killed.
Musselman was sentenced to life in prison. Musselman continued to claim innocence throughout the trial and after being found guilty by a jury.

While awaiting that trial, Musselman beat and killed a fellow inmate, Zakaria Sheek-Hussein, 27, at the Ottawa-Carleton Detention Centre during a fight on Feb 24, 2021. In September of this year, Musselman pleaded guilty to manslaughter. He was sentenced to another eight years in prison.

" This is a disturbing example of callous, extreme violence , " Superior Court Justice Kevin Phillips said during sentencing. " It's one thing to win a fight, it's quite another to stomp on the head of a man who has no fight left in him. "
